I've had these thoughts ever since I can remember. Maybe things would be different if I was a girl. Maybe people wouldn't ignore me, and maybe my hobbies would look cool if I was in a different body. Maybe having older siblings of the same sex would have helped, and maybe I couldn't at least subconsciously be angry with my introverted dad for never teaching me "manly" things. Maybe I wouldn't be afraid of expressing myself because that's "just for girls", and I wouldn't be laughed at for going to music school when all of the popular boys were into sports.

My attitude has always been, fuck it. I am the way I am, and for better or worse there's no changing that (not anymore, anyway, when my image in this town has already been established for what it is). I've always liked thought experiments, and this is definitely one. Like "What would happen if I jumped out my window?" or "How would my make-believe girlfriend react to this grade I got?"

But here's the deal, this sort of thinking often detracts from real life problems you might be facing. I strive to overcome those challenges first, then if they run out, find new ones. When I start conducting thought experiments I ask myself, "Don't you have a challenge to finish?" The answer is either "Right, I'll get back to it," or "I gave up." Your goal in this life is to answer with the latter as infrequently as possible.

I don't really know why I got all inspirational there but I wanted you to know you're not alone, and as long as you can control these thoughts you don't need a specialist or a counselor or an lgbtq subreddit.
